description: delimited-terminator's three records in a file whose last record carries no delimiter at all, which is what the optional-terminator placement admits. It is the entry the corpus's refusal to compare bytes was written for: a writer under this placement MUST emit the final delimiter rather than choosing whether to, so the twenty-three bytes here are written back as twenty-four and the two files decode to the same three records. What the placement gives up is stated with it -- a final record whose bytes were cut off is indistinguishable from one whose delimiter was never written -- and that is why this file is well-formed rather than truncated.
